  also at 12808330: 10063 passed, 107 skipped, 0 failed, 13 min 25 s. At the review head b23e5231, with the
  fragment rule, the neighbour files one at a time and the whole suite (10047 passed, 107 skipped) had passed
  too.
  `pre-commit run --files` on the changed files: all hooks passed; `ruff format --check` and `ruff check` (not a
  repository gate; there is no ruff configuration) clean on the two Python files this branch adds. Commits were
  made with `--no-verify` after the hooks ran by hand. Not run: CI's Python 3.12 (the local venv is 3.11), the
  Flutter jobs, `verify.sh` as a whole, any model call, any check against production.
- Durable learnings:
  - The worker's extraction child builds its run as a `SimpleNamespace` with `profile`, `dependencies`,
    `transcripts`, `fields`, `evidence` and `usage` only (`model_runtime.py` `_model_child`, line 68). Code in
    `apply_candidates` that reads `run.profile_snapshot` raises there, the child fails and the run blocks as
    `external_outcome_unknown`. Only `tests/test_model_runtime.py` shows it: my first version failed its first test
    there, and `origin/main`'s source passes it. The triage prototype used `getattr(run, "profile_snapshot", {})`
    for this reason. The guard now reads no run attribute at all, and the replay tests use a run of the child's shape.
  - `field_validators.date_parser` decides a slide code or a hyphen-joined part without the profile's date rules (it
    validates them first, line 85, and applies them only to a literal that is a date), so the refusal needs none;
    `test_the_date_refusal_does_not_depend_on_the_profile_date_rules` pins that for four rule sets and would fail
    if the parser ever used them for that decision.
  - The date rule follows the parser on pieces of hyphen-joined tokens too: the end of a hyphenated year range
    ("1948" in "1948-1950"), a part of a written day range ("12 Sept. 1946" or "10" in "10-12 Sept. 1946") and any
    date touching a hyphen-joined neighbour are refused, while the whole range literal ("10-12 Sept. 1946") is not.
    A hyphen-written day range ("IV-23-25-48") and an unspaced two-date range ("12-IV-48-15-IV-48", whole and at
    each end) are slide codes to the parser; a spaced range ("IV-23-48 - IV-25-48") is not refused. The date-shaped
    part of a code ("IV-29-68" in "IV-29-68-4") is `slide_code` by the HARNESS.md clause, not by
    GEOREFERENCING.md:173, which names whole codes. Tests pin each. No stored value is affected. Narrowing the
    date rule to `slide_code` alone is a one-line change if the owner does not want the rest.
  - A refused value reaches review only as the generic `mandatory_unresolved:{key}` reason (`policy.py:71`). The
    guard's own reason string is returned to the caller and recorded nowhere, so a reader of LAB.md:173-179 who looks
    for a kind-specific reason will not find one.
  - A guard on a literal's unit must read a mark after a range ("3300-3500 ft") as the unit of both ends and count
    only whole-number occurrences ("300" is not the tail of "1300" or "3,300"). The real label text has a comma
    straight before the number ("Yepocapa,4800 ft."): my first boundary refused any number after a comma and missed
    it, and the table test caught that.
  - A table test written as a dict silently drops a case whose name repeats (ruff F601 found two of mine); give
    each case its own name.
  - Limits the review listed, pinned by table cases: a slide code after other words ("H. Hoogstraal VI-24-68-7"),
    written with dots, or a literal that carries its own wrong unit ("3300 ft" in the metres field, left to the
    policy's Decimal reading and the derivations) passes the guard.
- Failed approaches: passing `run.profile_snapshot.get("date_rules")` into `date_parser`, as the brief said: it
  broke the extraction child (see the first learning). Refusing a proper fragment of a hyphen-joined token
  (`_enclosing_tokens`) in the four code-free fields: removed, see above.
- Remaining follow-ups: the owner's open questions: what Collection Code holds and where the top-edge code goes
  (including whether a piece of a slide-preparation code should ever be stored as Collection Code); whether a species
  or specimen number such as "Sp.#1" is a Taxon or Habitat value; they would add the refusals this PR leaves out (the
  FMNHINS prefix, the "Sp.#1" shape, a piece of a code). Giving the extractor the field meanings is separate. Whether
  the worker release rebuilds the job image on merge is Not confirmed (`docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:976` says the worker job
  is a follow-up).

  reader alternatives or supporting-source research; it cannot discard a fully
  admissible GBIF settlement. The same validator checks prospective settlement
  feedback; no model guess, checkpoint or side-effect is produced by that check.
  Genus-free sp.30 still makes no query; Danaus sp.30 remains a genus query.
- Taxonomy completion recovers only the exact failed query, not a different
  name's lookup from the same source. A cold completed capture replay resends
  nothing. An interrupted GBIF send retains its unknown hold and budget;
  correction/restart cannot bypass it.
- Helper admission bytes must be included in v4 acceptance fingerprinting.
  Hashing evidence.py alone allowed decisive taxonomy helper drift. V4 hashes
  an ordered pair of component digests with a version tag. The integrator must
  recompute the constant and corresponding Literal after composing changes from
  another lane to either component. This lane does not upgrade old job pins.

### 2026-10-09 — Claude: a reader failure is retried, then ends its reading, and never blocks the run (G6)

- Task: make a failed reader (`transcribe:`) step a known, retryable failure instead of `external_outcome_unknown`, which nothing in the product clears. Branch/worktree: `claude/reader-failures-recoverable` from `origin/main` e4f02e6b7, in an isolated Claude agent worktree; the pull request for this branch (#291) carries the evidence below. The operator "reconcile" action is another session's work and is not built here. This entry was revised once, before merge, after the independent reviewer's REQUEST CHANGES on head 29afb685f; the revision is part of this entry.
- Production evidence (read-only, from the lead): on 2026-10-09 the owner's new run on specimen 105526322 blocked at `transcribe:cf72bf96-...:handwriting-muse`, worker log 20:54:15Z `Specimen step failed ... branch=operational_block code=external_outcome_unknown ... error_class=OperationalBlock`. The cause of that run's child ending is Not confirmed (stderr is discarded by design); a reader's cap hit is the likeliest, a guess.
- Outcome: (1) #232's change re-applied on main (`ReadingStopped`; the reader maps `UsageLimitExceeded`; the child reports `stopped`; the `transcribe:` step completes with no observation) with its test `tests/test_reader_usage_limit.py`; its session-log entry was not copied. (2) `reliability.reader_failure_is_recoverable(run, step)` is the one predicate: a reader is a pure read, so every way it fails is a known failure. `model_runtime.child_without_answer` turns a child that ends as anything but an answer (deadline, kill, transport error, unmapped exception, unrecognised answer) into an `AdapterFailure` for a reader and keeps `external_outcome_unknown` for every other operation. The workflow's `AdapterFailure` handler drops the unknown flag for a reader, schedules the existing retry (429, 402, 5xx, timeout, deadline, malformed), and, when the last attempt fails, completes the step with no observation. `repeatable` starts true for a reader, so the deadline override neither restamps a retry nor drops the observation of a reader that answered late. (3) A request the provider refuses as invalid (HTTP 400, 404, 413, 422) is now `AdapterFailure("model_request_rejected", POLICY)` in `run_agent_bounded`, for every caller: it is never retried and blocks at once naming its cause, like 401/403 (402 stays transient). The first pass, the organiser and the legacy extraction call therefore also stop retrying those four statuses; their unknown outcomes are unchanged. (4) Every reading that gave no observation is recorded in `paid_calls` as `failed` with `failure_code` (`lane_costs.record_step(..., failure=)`), also when its step completed because it was given up on or stopped, with `cost_basis: reserved`. (5) A reader of the evidence pilot (`evidence_pilot` marker) is unchanged, including a stopped reading, which ends there as `external_outcome_unknown`: the cohort tests assert that an unknown reader never replays a paid call. (6) `integrity.verify_evidence` accepts a transcript with no text and no readings, because a region both readers failed on otherwise blocked at `parse` as `evidence_integrity_failure`; a transcript that holds text must still trace to a reading. To keep that rule from becoming a trap, the `transcription` decision in `api.py` refuses supported text for a region whose transcript has no readings (422, record unchanged); an abstention is still accepted. (7) `docs/execution/golive/HARNESS.md` section 3 states the rule, for the first pass and for readers.
- Validation actually run, Python 3.11 (`uv run`, CI uses 3.12), each file on its own, `TZ=America/Chicago`: new `tests/test_reader_failures_recoverable.py` (36 tests: eight retryable failure kinds through the real isolated child, a transient failure, a deadline, six non-retryable statuses that block and name their cause, the status mapping of `run_agent_bounded`, both readers failing, the refused human text and the accepted abstention, killed first-pass/organiser children still unknown, the reservation and the failed record of every attempt on a priced run, a stopped reading's record, a retry into `cost_budget_exhausted` and into `program_allowance_exhausted`, a pilot reader stopped by its limits); `tests/test_sam_retry.py` (a late answer keeps its observation; a reader past its budget is retried; first pass still waits); edited `test_model_runtime.py`, `test_model_runtime_tracing.py`, `test_reader_effect_timeout.py` (their transcribe cases asserted the old unknown outcome); pins `test_committed_pins`, `test_native_canonical_contract`, `test_native_canonical_v2_contract`, `test_canonical_materialization`, `test_canonical_materialization_v2`, `test_organiser_handover` (+ composer, engine), `test_enablement`, `tests/field_research/*`; about fifty neighbouring workflow, reliability, cost, pilot, lane, API and integrity files: results are in the pull request. Pre-fix proof: `git archive origin/main src` extracted to a scratch directory and put first on `PYTHONPATH` (the child inherits the parent's `sys.path`); on it 27 of the 50 tests in the new file and `test_sam_retry.py` fail, the rest are controls (401, 403, the budget and allowance blocks, text must trace, killed first-pass and organiser children, the unchanged statuses), plus the #232 tests and the edited tests. Not run: `scripts/ci/verify.sh`, the full suite, CI.
- Durable learnings: (1) `AdapterFailure.outcome_unknown` is a fact about the spend, and the block is policy; keep the policy in the workflow, keyed by one predicate, and the cost record unchanged (a reading with no observation records `cost_basis: reserved`, so every attempt's reservation stays held and nothing is refunded). (2) A region no reader read has a transcript with no readings, which evidence verification refused and which a reviewer's typed text would still hit; found only by driving both readers to fail, and reviewed into a refusal at the decision. (3) The deadline override fires on the success path too: `repeatable` must be true for a reader before the call, not set in the failure handlers. (4) The pilot cohort tests (`test_dynamic_pilot_reservations`, `test_stage_cost_reservations`) pin "an unknown reader never replays"; a change to readers must leave `evidence_pilot` runs alone or update those on purpose. (5) `tests/test_sam_retry.py` parametrised the deadline override over transcribe; it is now exercised for the first pass only. (6) A malformed reader answer costs two requests per attempt, so six requests over three attempts. (7) `model_request_rejected` uses `LookupStatus.POLICY`, which the provider circuit does not count as transient, so a rejected request does not open the breaker. (8) After merging #290 (reconcile), `tests/test_reconcile_ledger.py` made its unknown reader outcome with a provider `AdapterFailure(outcome_unknown=True)`, which a reader no longer leaves unknown; its fixture now raises a non-provider error after the request was sent (a parent-side exception on a reader still ends unknown, so reconcile still has readers to reconcile). `reconcilable_step` and the `reconcile` action are untouched.
- Considered and rejected: skipping the transcript of an unread region (the review action `transcription` raises "Unknown region" without it); blocking at `adjudicate` with a known code (retry could not re-open readers that were already complete without resetting attempt counters, which would collide with the program ledger's per-attempt keys).
- Remaining follow-ups for the lead and owner: `parse` still makes its extraction call when a run has no readings at all; the backoff is `retry_delay` (2-4 s, then 4-8 s), so a provider outage that outlasts those few seconds ends both readers' readings and sends the record to review rather than blocking, which is the owner's "an error occurred, retry" only through reprocess (a reviewer can only abstain on such a region); the stopped reading's tokens are still not returned from the child (#232's note); this applies to new runs after the runtime release and does not unblock runs already stuck as `external_outcome_unknown`.

Pins unchanged: `test_committed_pins` 19, `test_native_canonical_contract` 110, `test_native_canonical_v2_contract` 87, `test_canonical_materialization` 45, `test_canonical_materialization_v2` 50, `test_organiser_handover` 81 all pass. `flutter analyze` clean, `dart format` clean, `check_ui_strings.py` 0 violations, `pre-commit run --files` passed, both golden suites unchanged. `scripts/ci/verify.sh` was not run (shared machine); hosted CI Not confirmed at this entry.
- Reusable learnings: (1) the blocked step is `Workflow.next_step(run)`. A failed step never reaches `completed_steps`, and the intent save raises `run.attempts[step]` before the call, so `attempts[step] >= 1` is what ties an unknown blocker to its step. (2) A repeat is only safe after the lease expires, because the isolated model call is killed at its timeout well inside the lease; reconcile refuses while the lease is live and a stale worker's late `result:` save loses on the revision. (3) The program ledger key is `(specimen, run, step, attempt)` and `reserve_ordinary_liability` keys `step:attempt` from `attempts + 1`, so the re-run reserves under a new attempt and reconcile must never touch `usage`, `attempts`, `paid_calls` or either ledger. (4) Replay is not always 409. The checks run on the current record before `repository.save`, so a replay of a committed reconcile is refused with 409 while the run is no longer blocked. If the step blocks as unknown again and its lease expires, the same key and body pass the checks and reach the receipt path (`storage.py` `_commit`): the stored snapshot of the first reconcile comes back as a 200 with the old revision, and the record is not changed (`test_a_replay_after_the_step_blocks_again_returns_the_old_snapshot`). Only `reprocess` has a receipt-first replay (`replay_reprocess`, SQL Connect `execute`). (5) `parse` (the organiser) rewrites `run.fields` and appends evidence in place even when it fails, and honours preserved human fields, so it was left refused. (6) "Writes nothing outside the run" is too strong for a read: the isolated child writes content-addressed blobs before the run saves, and ending it does not cancel a request the provider already accepted (`bounded_effect.py`), so say "no record is written twice" and that a repeat may bill again. (7) In the app the Processing disclosure sits inside the closed Review details disclosure; a widget test opens Specimen data, then Review details, then Processing. `SemanticsHandle` must be disposed inside the test body, not in `addTearDown`. Worktree-isolated shells refuse heredocs and loops, so write scripts and messages to files.
- Failed approaches: the first 2.0x cut-off test used a fixture with no attempts or usage, so it missed that a real blocked run's `_Measurement` rows overflowed at 390 and 320 wide and that the drawer trigger "Execution policy, usage and attempts" was ellipsized. Fixed in the review round: the rows share the width 3 to 2 and wrap, and the trigger keeps the shared word "Technical detail" with the section in its spoken name; the test now carries attempts, usage and policy. The first workbench announcement test looked for the Processing disclosure at the top level.
- Follow-ups: decide whether the organiser step may be reconciled, after its in-place field and evidence handling is reviewed; a cancelled run with an unknown blocker still cannot be reprocessed (reprocess is refused while the blocker is unknown); an administrator reconciles the stuck run after release and the result is Not confirmed.

- In-flight jobs: a job's pins are rebuilt from the run's own `profile_snapshot` (`production_runtime.py` around line 216, `committed_pins.build_committed_pins`), a copy taken when the run is classified, not from the live registry. The profile digest reaches pins only as `owner_registration_digest` of the model price and request-bound rows (`committed_pins._harness_binding`). So a job pinned before this change rebuilds the same pins and is not held `research_committed_pins_changed`; a run queued after it gets the new snapshot, digest and allowance. The allowance a run enforces is the copy in `run.profile.execution.program_allowance_micros` that `lane.queue` takes from the published profile at intake and on the retry, resume and reprocess actions (`request_processing` in `application/api.py`), so a run in flight at the deploy keeps USD 5 until one of those actions queues it again. A ledger reservation records the allowance it was made under: if such a run then replays a step reserved under USD 5, `ProgramLedger.reserve` fails closed as `program_allowance_ledger_unavailable` and `ProgramLedger.settle` returns None, so the hold stays reserved and nothing is under-counted.
